question: When indifference is abandoned and agitation descends, which prior cognition of the phoneme-path applies in the Mother-portion?
premises: On the abandonment of indifference (audāsīnya) and on the descent of agitation (prakṣobha), the phoneme-path (varṇādhvā) is in play.
In the Mother-portion (mātṛbhāga) that valid cognition (pramā) would be the one previously stated (pūrvaṃ yā kathitā).
inference: The phoneme-path cognition already taught applies precisely at the transition from indifferent equipoise to agitated descent, within the Mother-portion.
uncertainties: varṇādhvā is glossed "color-path" by the drafter; in a11 it is the path of phonemes (varṇa = letter/sound), not colour — corrected here and flagged for review.
the referent of "previously stated" (pūrvaṃ … kathitā) must be fixed against the preceding verses; kept open rather than guessed.
plain_english: When indifference is abandoned and agitation descends, the path of phonemes comes into play; in the Mother-portion that valid cognition would be the one stated before.
